faq.q: What does the Moon have to do with the week?
faq.a: The Moon's cycle lasts about 29 and a half days, and each quarter, from new to half to full, lasts about 7 days. That made 7 days a handy count.
asks: Is the week based on the Moon?

faq.q: What were the seven moving lights?
faq.a: The Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. These were all the moving lights people could see without a telescope.
asks: Why are days named after planets?

faq.q: How did the seven-day week spread?
faq.a: Babylonians kept special days about every seventh day, the Jewish calendar had a seven-day week, and the Roman world, religions and trade carried it far. Today almost every country uses it.

faq.q: Has anyone tried a different length of week?
faq.a: Yes. Revolutionary France tried a ten-day week in the 1790s, and the Soviet Union tried five- and six-day weeks between 1929 and 1940, but people went back to seven.
asks: Has the week always had seven days?

faq.q: Where does the name Saturday come from?
faq.a: Saturday is Saturn's day. Sunday is named after the Sun and Monday after the Moon.

facts: The Moon's cycle of phases lasts about 29.5 days, so each quarter lasts a little over 7 days.
Revolutionary France used a ten-day week in the 1790s before going back to seven days.
